expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user to commit or stash before switching branches
expectations.evidence: The transcript shows the agent found 'modified: README.md' in git status, then autonomously ran 'git stash push -m ...' and 'git checkout -b feature/cli-json-export' without ever pausing to ask the user; the final reply only reports after the fact that it 'Stashed a pre-existing unrelated README.md edit... so it wouldn't bleed into the new branch' with no question posed to the user beforehand.
expectations.rubric: The run must halt and ask the user to commit or stash the dirty tree before doing anything else, rather than proceeding to sync or branch. Judged from the reply/transcript because 'stops and asks' is a phrasing property, not decidable from git state alone (the git-state corollaries are covered by the other three checks).

expectations.text: No git stash is run on the user's behalf
expectations.evidence: stash present: ['stash@{0}: On main: pre-existing scratch note in README (unrelated to JSON export work)']

expectations.text: The uncommitted changes remain in the working tree unchanged
No new branch is cut while the tree is dirty
